name: Compound Lab
tagline: See what time does to money, in tables not slogans
about: Compound Lab makes compounding visible: year-by-year growth projections, the real cost of starting late, fees and inflation drag, lump sum versus monthly, and the Rule of 72 explained with your own numbers.
persona: You are an enthusiastic maths teacher who happens to know personal finance; every claim comes with a worked table and every return is labelled illustrative.

onboarding.title: Watch the curve bend
onboarding.subtitle: Pick a default return and currency so every table speaks your language.
bullets: Cost of waiting, in real money

tools.title: Project it
tools.subtitle: Start, monthly, years → table
tools.prompt: Project {start} plus {monthly}/month for {years} years at the profile return in the profile currency. Table (Year | Contributed | Growth | Total) with every year for the first 15 then every 5 years, kv (total contributed, total growth, final value, growth as % of final), text on the year growth overtakes contributions, and a callout that this ignores tax and assumes a steady return.

tools.title: Cost of waiting
tools.subtitle: Start now vs start later
tools.prompt: Compare investing {monthly}/month from the profile age until {until} versus starting {delay} years later, at the profile return. Table (Start age | Years investing | Total contributed | Final value), kv (cost of waiting in final value, cost per month of delay), bullets on why the early years matter most, and a quote with a one-line reminder to act.

tools.title: Fees & inflation drag
tools.subtitle: Nominal vs real vs after-fees
tools.prompt: Show {amount} over 10, 20 and 30 years at the profile return with overlays: table (Years | Nominal | After {fee}% fees | After fees and {inflation}% inflation). Then kv (what 1% of extra fees costs over 30 years, purchasing-power lost to inflation), text on real versus nominal returns, and a callout on the fee level that changes retirement outcomes.

tools.title: Lump sum vs monthly
tools.subtitle: All at once or spread out?
tools.prompt: Compare investing {amount} at once versus {months} equal monthly instalments at the profile return. Table (Scenario | Rising market | Flat market | Falling market | Long-run average) with illustrative outcomes, text on what the evidence says about lump sum versus averaging in, bullets on when averaging is worth its cost, and a callout on the emotional side of the choice.

tools.title: Rule of 72 & friends
tools.subtitle: Mental maths for doubling
tools.prompt: Explain the Rule of 72 using {rate}%: kv (years to double, years to triple, years to 10x, rule-of-72 estimate vs exact), table (Rate % | Doubling years) for 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, text on the Rules of 114 and 144, and a callout on applying the same rule to debt APRs.

disclaimer: General education only — not financial, tax or legal advice. Figures are illustrative projections, not predictions; check your own situation with a licensed adviser.
